prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices, which transformed empirical industrial organisation and the evaluation of mergers and market power

statement.case_for: I moved my preferred part from B002, my opening first choice, to B001 after reading the other openings. The discovery is a single, well-defined methodological advance: random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices and equilibrium supply (BLP, 1995). It has three decades of use in academic work, merger review, antitrust and regulation, and it has spread to trade, health, environmental and public economics. The attribution is compact and can be defended in a citation. Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes wrote the demand-estimation paper, and Pakes also anchors the dynamic-industry and production-function strands. The work is fully mature. Its practical and conceptual reach is also broad enough to meet a common cross-field standard, not just an industrial-organisation one. The credibility questions I care about as an empirical labour economist, namely what is identified and under which assumptions, have been studied intensively for this method. Its sensitivities are documented and largely understood, which is a point in its favour. B002 and B013 remain strong alternatives, and I do not think B001's lead should be treated as a scientific verdict on them.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that this is a toolkit and a measurement framework, not a discovery about the world. Its results depend on functional-form and instrument assumptions, and applied estimates can be numerically fragile. The credited list has seven names, and the three-person cap forces an exclusion. Bresnahan, who pioneered the new empirical industrial organisation, is the most serious omission, and Benkard, Reiss and Levin also made adjacent contributions. A citation tied to BLP demand estimation fits the trio, but it leaves out the broader empirical-IO agenda. A reader could say the prize rewards one strand of a larger programme.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B001 first but names Bresnahan in the third slot alongside Pakes and Berry. He argues that Bresnahan's New Empirical IO and early differentiated-products demand work make him at least as strong a co-contributor as Levinsohn. He also proposes only Kiyotaki and Moore for B002, to avoid the overlap with the 2022 prize.
responses.response: I proposed Bresnahan in my opening and take the argument seriously. Bresnahan's contribution is a research programme and a way of thinking about market power. It is not the demand-estimation method. The achievement the Committee can cite most precisely is BLP, and Levinsohn is a co-author of that paper. If the citation names the method, the attribution is cleaner with the BLP trio. I now think the Bresnahan case is better handled by a broader citation, which this three-person cap does not allow. On B002, I agree that adding Gertler imports the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist strand and the 2022 overlap. If B002 is the preferred part, the cleaner version is Kiyotaki and Moore, and I would qualify my own opening trio accordingly.

responses.point: Hassler sees the BLP framework as a compact, clear core and a three-person set as natural. He notes that the field has not been recognised as a structural-estimation tradition, so timing is ripe. He is also uncertain whether the contribution reads as method or as economic discovery.
responses.response: I agree on the compact attribution and the timing. On method versus discovery, I think the answer is that the method changed what economists can say about substitution, market power and welfare in real markets. It is not a tool in the abstract. That is a discovery-enabling contribution of the same type the Academy has honoured in causal inference. I also take your point on B002. Your two-person Kiyotaki-Moore proposal and your view that adding Gertler dilutes a clean pair make me less confident in my own three-name B002 trio.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B013 first. She argues it combines an explanatory framework with new empirical designs and large policy impact, and she flags that Dorn is omitted only because of the three-name cap. She also notes the open choice between the task framework and the trade-shock design as the core.
responses.response: I share your view that B013 is credible, empirically and in societal importance. I ranked it third and kept it as an alternative. My hesitation is that the contribution splits into two strands with different cores. The task and skill-premium literature rests on Autor and Katz, and the China-shock evidence rests on Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The magnitude and persistence of the shock effects are still contested. So a three-name citation either excludes Dorn, who is a core author of the trade-shock papers, or has to compress two achievements. B001 does not have the same attribution split. I would reconsider B013 if the Committee settles which strand is the achievement.

uncertainties: Whether Levinsohn or Bresnahan should take the third slot, and whether the Committee prefers a narrow BLP citation or a broader empirical-IO framing.
Whether the Committee treats structural estimation as a discovery-enabling contribution or as method only.
How much the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises should reduce the case for B002, and whether Gertler should be credited alongside Kiyotaki and Moore.
Whether the long-run magnitudes of the China-shock effects in B013 are settled enough, and whether Dorn can be excluded under the cap.
I rely on background knowledge and on the colleagues' openings for citation and adoption claims, and I have not independently verified them.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie with any credited name on B001, B002 or B013. My profile ties are to the Uppsala and IFAU labour-economics network, and none of these candidates are in it. The 2021 Scientific Background cites my class-size paper, but that does not relate to these candidates.
